scope: Review new workload search, per-die throughput allocation and result interpretation; recheck prior pin sampling/input-identity fixes. Production code unchanged.

findings.problem: Front coordinates are loaded from NPZ but nominal lengths and peaks are copied from a separate summary without binding or independently checking the actual layout. These stale values determine feasibility and the nominal-best baseline.

negative_control.method: Real FV and geometry computations; replace expensive stochastic searches with one known layout and execute pools serially. Admission/selection/reporting code unchanged.

findings.impact: A valid but replaced layout with actual length 7 mm is admitted under a 6.25 mm cap as 5 mm; reported nominal peak also differs from its actual FV peak. Regret/reverse-cost comparisons can therefore mix different physical layouts and constraints.
findings.fix_direction: Before selection, bind the layout artifact to the frozen front and recompute its lengths/nominal peaks against the summary. Case JSON hashing alone does not identify NPZ coordinates.

findings.problem: An infeasible coolest baseline and feasible alternative produce loss=None, which is dropped. If every loss is None, all() over the empty list returns True and the tool declares degenerate.

negative_control.method: Synthetic passive linear response matrices; production LP, selection, loss and verdict unchanged.

findings.impact: The control has a nominally cooler 100 C layout with infeasible fixed-memory heating, while a nominally hotter 101 C alternative supports positive compute. The tool records a feasible best but aggregates the case as degenerate when it is the only comparison. It confuses missing comparisons/feasibility gains with evidence of no benefit.
findings.fix_direction: Report baseline-infeasible/alternative-feasible separately from wholly infeasible cases, retain its feasibility gain, and emit insufficient-data when no comparable cases remain rather than degenerate.

findings.problem: Double argsort gives distinct ordinal ranks to ties, so the quantity labeled Spearman is not tie-correct and may depend on row order.

negative_control.method: All layouts admit X_MAX; production LP and ranking arithmetic unchanged.

findings.impact: Three layouts at 75/65/55 C all saturate X_MAX and have identical throughput 11.4471424255, yet the output reports Spearman=1. Throughput is constant, so correlation is undefined; a saturated region can be misread as a perfect ordering relationship.
findings.fix_direction: Use average ranks or scipy.stats.spearmanr, and store an explicit undefined/null result for constant inputs.

package.nominal_heat_transfer_monotonicity: passed for h and TIM variants

saved_results.provenance: Both tool source hashes, all 20 summary bindings, all front-index sequences and all ten local case identities match.
saved_results.scope: Independent saved-table arithmetic and invariant checks, not full thermal-field replay; new coupling search and throughput results were not published at analyzed HEAD.

limitations: Synthetic controls establish implementation failures, not their frequency in real input data.

The workload-search control replaces the expensive stochastic search with a single known layout; FV and geometry are computed normally. The throughput controls provide known passive linear response matrices; LP, selection, ranking and verdict code are unchanged.
No coupling-search or throughput-results artifact is published at analyzed HEAD; no claim is made that an already-running external campaign encountered these failures.
Existing package/workload metrics were checked from saved arrays, not by rerunning all 1340 thermal layouts.
The reduced package and throughput models remain uncalibrated; passing numerical checks does not qualify actual hardware.
